cards.front: Recall a key point about Nazi Consolidation of Power
cards.back: On 27 February 1933, the Reichstag building in Berlin was set on fire. Marinus van der Lubbe, a Dutch Communist, was found at the scene and arrested. Hitler used the fire to persuade Hindenburg to issue the Decree for the Protection of the People and State on 28 February 1933, which suspended all civil liberties.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Nazi Consolidation of Power
cards.back: In the March 1933 election, the Nazis won 43.9% of the vote (288 seats). This was not a majority, but combined with the DNVP's 8% (52 seats), Hitler had a majority in the Reichstag. The election was held in an atmosphere of terror - SA thugs patrolled the streets, opposition meetings were banned, and the Communist Party was effectively illegal.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Nazi Consolidation of Power
cards.back: The Enabling Act (Law to Remedy the Distress of the People and the Reich), passed on 23 March 1933, gave Hitler the power to make laws without the Reichstag for four years. This effectively made Hitler a legal dictator. It required a two-thirds majority, which Hitler achieved by arresting Communists and intimidating the remaining deputies.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Nazi Consolidation of Power
cards.back: On 14 July 1933, the Law Against the Formation of New Parties made the NSDAP the only legal political party in Germany. Attempting to form or maintain another party became a criminal offence. Germany was now a one-party state.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Nazi Consolidation of Power
cards.back: On 29-30 June 1934, Hitler ordered the SS to murder the leadership of the SA, including its head Ernst Röhm. At least 85 people were killed, including former Chancellor von Schleicher and other conservative critics. The SA's power was broken and the SS (under Himmler) became the dominant force in Nazi terror.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Nazi Consolidation of Power
cards.back: By August 1934, Hitler had achieved total power: the Reichstag was powerless; all other parties were banned; trade unions were abolished; the SA was neutered; the army had sworn personal loyalty; and he combined the roles of President and Chancellor. Germany was now a totalitarian dictatorship.

cards.front: What should you know about history exam tips — nazi consolidation of power?
cards.back: 1. For Nazi Consolidation of Power, include specific factual detail: dates, names, events and statistics where relevant 2. For source questions, analyse provenance (who, when, why, audience) before using the content 3. In evaluation questions, discuss multiple factors and weigh their relative significance 4. Always link back to the question focus — don't just narrate what happened with Nazi Consolidation of Power 5. Use phrases like 'the most significant factor was... because...' to show analytical judgement
KPD effectively banned (deputies arrested) (e.g. Communist opposition eliminated)
Trade unions abolished; leaders arrested (e.g. Workers' organisations destroyed; replaced by German Labour Front (DAF))
SPD offices seized; assets confiscated (e.g. Social Democratic opposition ended)
SPD formally banned (e.g. Last major left-wing party gone)
Other parties "voluntarily" dissolved (DVP, DDP, BVP, DNVP) (e.g. Only the Nazi Party remained)
Law Against the Formation of New Parties (e.g. Nazi Party declared the only legal party in Germany)
